facts.claim: Apple said in June 2024 that its on-device model has about 3 billion parameters, stored at an average of 3.7 bits per weight, and writes about 30 tokens a second on an iPhone 15 Pro.

Apple’s July 2025 report says it trained its roughly 3-billion-parameter on-device model to work at 2 bits per weight, and that letting one block of layers reuse another’s keys and values cut its KV cache memory by 37.5%.
Google said in June 2025 that Gemma 3n’s two phone models, with 5 and 8 billion parameters in all, run in as little as 2 GB and 3 GB of memory.
Meta’s Llama 3.2 model card lists its small models at 1.23 and 3.21 billion parameters, made for constrained places such as mobile devices.
Llama 3.2 1B keeps 16 layers of 8 key-value heads of 64 numbers each; the 3B keeps 28 layers of 8 heads of 128, as their published configs give.
Meta said in October 2024 that its quantized Llama 3.2 1B and 3B were 56% smaller and used 41% less memory on a OnePlus 12 phone, and that interactions stay entirely on the device.
Laskaridis et al. (MELTing point, 2024) measured 0.16 to 0.21 mWh per token for 3-billion-parameter models on phones: about 490 to 590 replies of 135 tokens on one full battery.
In the same study, an iPhone 14 Pro running a 4-bit 3B model reached 47.9 °C, and over 50 prompts in a row its speed kept dropping as the phone changed power modes.
Apple calls on-device processing the cornerstone of its users’ privacy; requests that need a larger model go to its Private Cloud Compute, which keeps no user data after replying (June 2024).
